upper motor neuron

Introduction

Tongue fasciculations, with electrophysiologically confirmed denervation, strongly support a diagnosis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in bulbar presentations, although mimics have been reported [1]. While “tongue tremor” or rhythmic movements have been described in progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) [2, 3], genuine fasciculations with electrophysiologically confirmed denervation are not expected.

title: Assessing mental resilience with individual and lifestyle determinants among nursing students: An observational study from Greece
creator: Maria Antoniou, Evangelos C Fradelos, Theano Roumeliotaki, Foteini Malli, Emmanouil, K Symvoulakis, Dimitrios Papagiannis
description: The educational environment is important for the development of life skills of nursing students in late- and post-adolescence. Strengthening their mental resilience, enhancing their individual confidence, and controlling stress are necessary conditions in this direction, which will help them cope with the future challenges of their chosen profession.

title: Effect of school-based HPV vaccine campaigns on inequalities in uptake in France: the PrevHPV trial
creator: J Dussault, A S Le Duc-Banaszuk, A Gagneux-Brunon, S Bruel, A Gauchet, A S Barret, J Sicsic, N Thilly, J E Mueller, PrevHPV consortium
description: BackgroundHPV vaccination is recommended in France for all adolescents aged 11-14. Coverage has increased over recent years but remains below 50% by age 15, with social disparities by area deprivation level, parental education and income. We analysed the effect of school-wide campaigns on adolescent vaccine uptake and related disparities.

title: CircHMGA2 facilitates proliferation and invasion of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma cells and M2 macrophage polarization via the miR-384/ROCK1 axis
creator: Zhenjun Wang, Ping Wu, Li Li, XianHua Zhu, Yueyong Xiao
description: IntroductionLaryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) is a malignant tumor of the head and neck. CircRNA High Mobility Group AT-hook 2 (circHMGA2) has cancer-promoting functions. Nevertheless, the role of circHMGA2 in LSCC has not been reported yet. We attempted to illustrate the function and mechanism of circHMGA2 in LSCC.

title: Transvenous extraction and reimplantation procedures for quadripolar left ventricular leads with an active fixation side helix
creator: Takehiro Nomura, Tsuyoshi Isawa, Shigeru Toyoda, Kennosuke Yamashita, Taku Honda
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Five ASQ extraction cases from our hospital were showed in this list. All leads were completely removed and there were no serious complications. Laser sheaths were used in four of the five cases.

title: General and special education teachers’ readiness for artificial intelligence in classrooms: A structural equation modeling study of knowledge, attitudes, and practices in select UAE public and private schools
creator: Mohammad Fteiha, Mohammad Al-Rashaida, Mohammed Ghazal
description: As artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes global education systems, understanding educators’ readiness to integrate AI into classroom practices is essential. This study examines the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of general and special education teachers in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) regarding AI in education.

title: Exploring the potential of tocols and retinoids in authenticating pasture-derived sheep milk and cheese
creator: Nagore Iglesias-Rodrigo, María Ángeles Bustamante, Noelia Aldai, Paz Lavín, Teresa Manso, Ángel R Mantecón, Luis Javier R Barron
description: This study investigated the potential of tocols and retinoids to differentiate sheep milk and cheese from concentrate-feeding indoor farms and pasture-feeding extensive farms. A total of 94 milk and 90 cheese samples collected from intensive and extensive commercial farms were analyzed using high-performance liquid chromatography to quantify α- and γ-tocopherol, α- and β-tocotrienol, retinyl palmitate, and retinol.

title: Community health needs in Ukraine in the war context
creator: A Fenchak, A Gerasimova
description: The full-scale russia's invasion in Ukraine caused the migration of people, partially destroyed the medical infrastructure, disrupted access to services, so there is a need to connect people tocare. The e-tools allow to monitor the capacities of the healthcare system and utilization of services. However, there is insufficient data on the population's needs.

title: Evaluating pre-consult patient education videos for patients with newly-diagnosed anal squamous cell carcinoma: Impact on patient comprehension, satisfaction and distress
creator: Kelsey L Corrigan, Lauren M Andring, Prajnan Das, Cheryl Pfennig, Kimberly B Porter, Ethan B Ludmir, Sonal S Noticewala, Bruce D Minsky, Grace L Smith, Eugene J Koay, Albert C Koong, Angelica Arzola, Sarah J Lee, LaShon Nelms, Emma B Holliday
description: Highlights•Radiation for anal cancer is complex, stressful and can cause side effects.•Pre-consult videos improve patient understanding on key content.•Patient satisfaction was high and distress scores at content were low. Introduction Squamous cell carcinoma of the anus (SCCA) is a rare malignancy, and pelvic radiation therapy (RT) with concurrent chemotherapy is curative for the majority of patients [1], [2].

title: Comparison, by Country, of the Uptake of COVID-19 Vaccination by Health Care Workers in the EU/EEA
creator: T McGlacken, M Codd
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Health Care Workers (HCWs) are at high risk of exposure to COVID-19 when providing care to patients. We investigated the uptake of COVID-19 vaccination among HCWs in the EU/EEA and discuss the factors which influence this uptake.- The aim of this study was to compare, by country, COVID-19 vaccination uptake by HCWs from January to June 2021, to assist with policy making and prospective planning in these countries during the current pandemic and into the future.

title: Behavioral and environmental drivers of dairy performance in alpine grazing cows managed with precision livestock farming technologies
creator: Marta Pavolini, Giulia Gislon, Maddalena Zucali, Alberto Tamburini, Anna Sandrucci
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Dairy farming on mountain pastures is a traditional activity that is declining due to the numerous challenges posed by mountain environments. For 2 summer seasons (2024 and 2025), the feeding behaviors of a herd of Bruna breed cows (20 lactating cows in 2024, 8 primiparous and 12 multiparous; 25 in 2025, 8 primiparous and 17 multiparous) on the Italian Alps were investigated, together with milk production, milk composition, and pasture quality and availability.

title: Methods of a cluster-randomized, type II hybrid implementation effectiveness trial to prospectively assess extended-duration thromboprophylaxis for at-risk medical patients being discharged to prevent hospital-associated venous thromboembolism
creator: Scott C Woller, Scott M Stevens, Joseph R Bledsoe, James Hellewell, Adam Kraft, Allison M Butler, Masarret Fazili, James F Lloyd, Paige S Christensen, Ithan D Peltan, Geoffrey D Barnes, Benjamin D Horne
description: BackgroundVenous thromboembolism (VTE) is the third leading cause of preventable hospital-associated (HA) death. Most HA-VTE, including fatal pulmonary emboli, occur among medically ill patients. The rate of symptomatic VTE more than doubles over the first 21 days after hospital discharge. Trials have demonstrated that the burden of HA-VTE may be reduced with postdischarge thromboprophylaxis; however, few patients receive this therapy.

title: Impact of digital intervention on antenatal paper records: results from audit of antenatal records
creator: S Das, E Radovich, S Karki, R Shakya, A Shrestha, B Karmacharya, L Penn-Kekana, O McCarthy, O Campbell, A Shrestha
description: BackgroundGood recordkeeping is important in antenatal care (ANC). The mIRA study aimed to improve ANC quality through tablet-based electronic decision support systems (EDSS). Electronic data entry was implemented alongside existing paper-based ANC records, adding an additional record-keeping requirement for health care providers. This study assesses the impacts of the EDSS on paper-based ANC records.

title: Farmer experiences with virtual fencing: Adoption, adaptation, and farm system change in New Zealand pasture-based dairy systems
creator: Callum R. Eastwood, Brian Dela Rue, Lucy Hall
description: Virtual fencing (VF) is a livestock management technology that uses global positioning systems–enabled collars and audio or electrical cues to geo-fence and herd animals. Virtual fencing is now in use on farms in several countries; however, there have been limited studies on the use of VF on commercial dairy farms and assessing the implications for how farm systems are managed.

title: Osteoclast indices in osteogenesis imperfecta: systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Sirion Aksornthong, Priyesh Patel, Svetlana V Komarova
description: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a rare bone fragility disorder caused by mutations in genes encoding collagen type I or that affect its processing. Alterations in osteoclasts were suggested to contribute to OI pathophysiology. We aimed to systematically identify studies reporting measures of osteoclast formation and function in patients and mouse models of OI, to quantify OI-induced changes.

title: Functional social support and physical activity in community-dwelling older adults: A scoping review
creator: P Steinhoff, A Reiner
description: BackgroundGlobally, the population of older people is increasing and is estimated to reach nearly 2.1 billion by 2050. Physical activity (PA) is one of the key components for healthy ageing, as it can prevent noncommunicable diseases, improve mental health, cognitive functioning and quality of life. However, PA decreases with age.

title: Self-regulated optomechanics achieves ultrabroadband and high-efficiency all-optical devices
creator: Xuning Wang, Guodong Hou, Feiyu Zhang, Feihong Du, Ruhong Luo, Zhenhua Ma, Yezhan Lin, Chunyu Wang, Yifan Zhao, Binzhou Sun, Cenling Huang, Lu Yu, Shanyu Zheng, Qiang Li, Donglin Han, Haixin Qiu, Jiang Zou, Xin Chen, Tiannan Yang, Wei Li, Weihong Zhu, Xiangyang Zhu, Di Zhang, Yanqing Lu, Guang Meng,
description: All-optical logic devices require nonreciprocal wave propagation, which is often achieved by resonance or nonlinear effects at the cost of limited transmitted modes, wavelengths, and overall energy efficiency. By leveraging the inherited feedback loops, the nature-inspired self-regulated soft actuators could act as “gatekeepers” to identify the wave propagation direction to achieve similar logic functions in linear optics.

title: Flu vaccination ‘influenced’ by Covid-19: Italy experience
creator: R Iannaccone, L Dragoni, G Messina, N Nante
description: BackgroundDuring last decades, National Health System has guaranteed free flu vaccination to the ‘fragile’ population. However, the population's compliance with this prophylactic procedure has never been optimal, reaching only in a few years and only in some regions the percentage considered satisfactory of 70% of people at risk.

title: Local adaptation sustains genetic differentiation between two varieties of Chinese walnut (Juglans cathayensis) despite extensive hybridization in subtropical China
creator: Wan Hu, Caixia Han, Li Li, Chunhua Zang, Runzi Li, Hong Nie, Jianbo Nie, Yong Shi, Chen Feng, Jie Zhang, Yixuan Kou, Zhiyong Zhang, Dengmei Fan, Danqi Li
description: Understanding how natural selection sustains genetic differentiation despite ongoing hybridization remains a central question in evolutionary biology. Here, we integrated range-wide whole-genome resequencing data and ecological niche modeling to elucidate the evolutionary history, local adaptation, and hybridization patterns of Juglans cathayensis, a walnut species widely distributed across subtropical China.

title: The role of gender composition in workplace sexual harassment
creator: N P Larsson, L Craven, IEH Madsen
description: BackgroundWorkplace sexual harassment is associated with adverse mental health consequences and research suggests that gender minority status may be a risk factor. We analysed the prevalence of workplace sexual harassment in male and female-dominated-occupations to elucidate the role of gender minority status.

title: Mothers’ perceptions of barriers and opportunities for health-promoting lifestyle one year postpartum
creator: B Fuchs-Neuhold, S Holasek
description: BackgroundPregnancy is often seen as an opportunity for women to transition to a health-promoting lifestyle but maintaining healthy habits can be challenging in the postpartum period. This study aims to explore women's experiences with lifestyle changes related to diet, physical activity, mental health, and social health one year after delivery.

title: WHO Support tool to strengthen health information systems
creator: D Novillo-Ortiz
description: In the first presentation, a representative of the WHO Europe team who took part to the development of the “Support tool to strengthen health information systems: guidance for health information system assessment and strategy development” as part of the European Health Information Initiative (EHII), will introduce the tool and the relevance of performing health information system assessments to support Member

title: Sick at work and future sickness absence - a prospective study of two measures of sickness presence
creator: C D Hansen, L Dalgaard, T N Winding, J H Andersen
description: BackgroundSickness presence (SP), or going to work despite being ill, is a common way of practicing sickness absence (SA). However, its consequences for long-term SA are poorly understood, and there is no consensus on how to measure SP. This study aims to examine the consequences of SP on long-term sickness absence (>14 days) using two different measures.

title: Association between PFAS and renal function indicators in cord blood of newborns: modifying effects of newborn sex and maternal factors
creator: Wu Yan, Penghong Xu, Ying Xu, Wentao Yang, Qian Huang, Sabitina Mrisho Mzava, Francis Manyori Bigambo, Dandan Wang, Xu Wang
description: BackgroundEvidence on the associations between per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) exposure and renal function in newborns remains limited, particularly in cord blood studies. This retrospective cross-sectional study aimed to explore the associations between individual and mixed PFAS exposure with renal function indicators in the cord blood and to examine whether these associations were modified by newborn sex and maternal factors.

title: Quality of life and Job satisfaction in medical specialists
creator: K Ordaz Lopez, J M Quevedo Flores, G J Trujillo Peña, O Viveros Sosa, J S Villegas Dominguez
description: BackgroundFollowing the COVID-19 pandemic, the outlook for many physicians changed unexpectedly. There is evidence indicating that clinical performance decreases in stressed physicians, or with job dissatisfaction, factors that influence your quality of life.ObjectiveTo determine the correlation between quality of life and job satisfaction in medical specialists in Veracruz, Mexico.

title: Organ‐Specific Cancer‐Associated Fibroblast Subtypes Across the Digestive System Linked to Cancer Hallmarks
creator: Huaitao Wang, Takashi Semba, Atsuko Yonemura, Hiroshi Naito, Lingfeng Fu, Takuya Tajiri, Masaaki Iwatsuki, Takatsugu Ishimoto
description: Cancer‐associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are major stromal components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) and play diverse roles in gastrointestinal (GI) cancer progression, immunity, and therapeutic resistance. However, the heterogeneity, tissue specificity, and clinical relevance of CAFs across GI cancers remain incompletely defined. We integrated 14 independent single‐cell RNA‐sequencing datasets comprising 239 GI adenocarcinoma samples to define the subtypes of CAFs.

title: Combined Lifestyle Intervention to reduce overweight at the workplace: opinions of stakeholders
creator: P Beurskens, I Houkes, G Norder, A de Rijk
description: BackgroundOverweight is a risk factor for employee health and sustainable employability. Multifactorial interventions, addressing both the employee's individual lifestyle and the work environment, are expected to be most effective in overweight reduction. In the Netherlands, primary care patients with overweight are referred to Combined Lifestyle Interventions (CLI), but this is not yet common in occupational health.

title: Comorbidity Patterns Between Hearing Loss and Symptomatic Dizziness in Middle‐Aged and Older Adults
creator: Chun‐Yan Liu, Xiao‐Nan Wu, Jin Li, Jiao Zhang, Yun Gao, Da‐Yong Wang, Qiu‐Ju Wang
description: ObjectiveTo explore the comorbidity patterns between hearing loss and symptomatic dizziness (HL‐SD) in middle‐aged and older adults.MethodsThis cross‐sectional study used data from the 1999 to 2004 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). After excluding incomplete data, 2961 participants aged 40–69 were analyzed.

title: Trends in acute hospital smoking prevalence and support of campus ban in Dublin, Ireland (1997-2018)
creator: A Mattson, A Lyons, K Doherty, A Douglass, S Stynes, M Kerley, P Fitzpatrick, C Kelleher
description: BackgroundSt Vincent's University Hospital (SVUH), a major hospital in Dublin, Ireland pioneered a hospital smoke-free campus policy in 2009; pre/post this intervention it conducted periodic surveys of patients, staff & visitors for smoking prevalence and policy attitudes. As rates of smoking decline nationally in Ireland, it is important to monitor trends for at-risk groups, including lower socioeconomic status (SES).

title: Sociodemographic Characteristics Associated with PCSK9 Inhibitor Use in Individuals with Possible Familial Hypercholesterolemia in Alberta: A Cohort Study
creator: Samuel E Fineblit, David M Vickers, David JT Campbell
description: BackgroundProprotein convertase subtilisin/kinase type 9 inhibitors (PCSK9is) significantly lower low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-c) level and improve cardiovascular outcomes, but they remain underutilized, potentially due to access-related barriers. This study examines clinical and sociodemographic factors associated with PCSK9i prescriptions in Alberta, Canada.MethodsA population-based study was conducted using data from the Alberta Kidney Disease Network.

title: Five years after the Earthquake and nuclear accident: Loss and its psychological effect
creator: Y Tsuchiya, T Tsujiuchi
description: BackgroundOn March 11, 2011, the Great East Japan Earthquake hit Tohoku. The Fukushima nuclear power plant accident forced many people to relocate, leaving their hometowns. This study focused on the sense of loss and its psychological effect on the people of Fukushima five years after the earthquake and nuclear accident.

title: Assessing the real-world safety of docetaxel for non-small cell lung cancer: Insights from a comprehensive analysis of FAERS data
creator: Lei Wang, Hui Zhao, Kunpeng Yang, Zhe Wang, Chenglun Cai, Peiyun Lv, Bao Wang, Guocan Yu, Guocan Yu, Guocan Yu
description: BackgroundDocetaxel is a key therapeutic agent in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but comprehensive real-world data on its adverse effects remain scarce. This study aims to evaluate docetaxel-related adverse drug events by analyzing the Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) from 2004 to 2024.

title: Artificial Intelligence Chatbots for medical training in Public Health: a tool to explore
creator: F Baglivo, L De Angelis, V Casigliani, G Arzilli, G P Privitera, C Rizzo
description: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) is a rapidly developing field with the potential to transform various aspects of healthcare and public health including medical training. During the ‘Hygiene and Public Health’ course for fifth-year medical students, a practical training session was conducted on vaccination using AI as an educational supportive tool.

title: Effect of Tonsillar Retractor on Intracranial and Intraocular Pressure in Children Undergoing Adenotonsillectomy Surgeries
creator: Ayse Bozkurt Oflaz, Meltem Isık, Merih Onal, Mete Kaan Bozkurt, Ozkan Onal, Banu Bozkurt
description: ObjectivesThe tonsillar retractor used during adenotonsillectomy, one of the most common pediatric surgeries, may increase sympathetic activity. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of tonsillar retractor insertion on intracranial pressure (ICP) and intraocular pressure (IOP) in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.MethodsThis prospective observational study included 24 pediatric patients undergoing adenotonsillectomy and 20 age‐matched controls undergoing other surgeries.

title: Artificial Intelligence Electrocardiogram-Derived Heart Age Predicts Long-Term Mortality After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement
creator: Ghasaq Saleh, Agata Sularz, Chia-Hao Liu, Gerardo V Lo Russo, Mahmoud Zhour Adi, Zachi Attia, Paul Friedman, Rajiv Gulati, Mohamad Alkhouli
description: Central Illustration Age significantly influences the risk of cardiovascular (CV) disease. However, chronological age may not always align with CV age, a disparity referred to as the “age gap.” Various methods, including genetic, cellular, and biochemical techniques, have been utilized to estimate CV age.

title: Anticancer peptides as novel immunomodulatory therapeutic candidates for cancer treatment
creator: Apurva Sood, VV Jothiswaran, Amrita Singh, Anuradha Sharma, Jianxun Ding
description: Cancer remains a concern after years of research in this field. Conventional therapies such as chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery are available for cancer treatment, but they are characterized by various side effects. There are several immunological challenges that make it difficult for the immune system and conventional therapies to treat cancer.

title: Approaches to tracing the geographic origin of wildlife trade
creator: Tong Tong Gu, Hao Zhang, Yu Xin He, Jing Yang Hu, Li Yu
description: illegally traded species and determine the origin of confiscated wild animals and their products, thereby assisting law enforcement agencies in tracing the sources of the trafficking. Here, we summarize the current analytical approaches used to trace the geographical origin of species, including trade record, elemental signature, and molecular genetics analyses (Fig. 1).

title: Homozygous SGCB splice-site variant causes isolated dilated cardiomyopathy through sarcoglycan complex destabilization in East Asians
creator: Fangfang Li, Haruki Shinomiya, Yuki Kuramoto, Koshiro Kanaoka, Yuji Sakahashi, Yasuki Ishihara, Hidetaka Kioka, Seiko Ide, Yumi Yamaguchi-Kabata, Shu Tadaka, Ikuko N. Motoike, Kengo Kinoshita, Kinuko Ohneda, Hidetoshi Sakurai, Takahiro Okumura, Yohei Miyashita, Kota Jojima, Hisakazu Kato, Ken Matsuo
description: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a genetically heterogeneous disorder, characterized by ventricular dilatation and impaired systolic function, leading to heart failure and sudden cardiac death. Despite advances in genomic technologies, the genetic cause of DCM remains unidentified in more than half of the cases.

title: The impact of HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis on sexually transmitted infections incidence in Bulgaria
creator: I Pakov, E Birindzhieva, A Milanov, K Terzieva, G Gancheva
description: BackgroundThe global introduction of effective Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) alongside with available antiretroviral medications against HIV strongly limited the spread of infection among the high-risk population. This remarkable success predisposes to riskier sexual behaviour and has emerged as leading cause of the increased incidence of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in sizes of new threatening pandemic.

title: Bilateral Three-Port Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Thymectomy for Thymoma in Good’s Syndrome With a History of Bacteremia
creator: Ryo Shibayama, Sakashi Fujimori, Souichirou Suzuki, Reo Ohtsuka, Takahiro Karasaki
description: A 62-year-old man presented with back pain, lower leg swelling, and fever and was referred to our hospital. Blood cultures identified Helicobacter fennelliae as the causative agent of bacteremia associated with pyogenic spondylitis and cellulitis. CT revealed a tumor in the upper anterior mediastinum, and blood tests showed low gamma globulin levels, raising the suspicion of Good’s syndrome.

title: A cluster of Histamine Fish Poisoning associated with the ingestion of tuna
creator: T McGlacken, S Kelly, K O'Connor, H Murray, C Mullaney
description: Histamine fish poisoning, also known as scombroid poisoning, arises from the improper handling and refrigeration of scombroid fish that contain naturally occurring histidine such as tuna, mackerel and swordfish. Histidine is converted to histamine when these fish inadequately chilled. Histamine fish poisoning is generally associated with levels greater than 500 mg/kg but poisonings have been observed at lower levels (e.g.

title: Temperature around conception and metabolic health in adulthood: Evidence from the UK Biobank
creator: T Münz, F Pradella, L Gerking, S Gabrysch, R van Ewijk
description: BackgroundMice studies and correlational evidence among humans suggest that paternal cold exposure around conception is associated with improved metabolic outcomes among the offspring, which is caused by an increase in their amount of active brown fat. Especially the 2 weeks prior to conception are relevant as epigenetic programming during spermatogenesis takes place. Causal evidence on humans is thus far lacking.

title: RETRACTION: Isolation of Antidiabetic Principle from Fruit Rinds of Punica granatum
creator: Evidence-Based Complementary and Alternative Medicine
description:
Library (https://www.wileyonlinelibrary.com), has been retracted by John Wiley & Sons Ltd. The retraction has been agreed due to figure concerns initially identified on PubPeer [1]. Specifically, in Figure 5, images C and E appear to have been duplicated, resized, and rotated, despite the different experimental conditions indicated. The results and conclusions are therefore considered unreliable.

The authors did not respond when notified of the retraction.

title: Building Community Health Literacy with a Social Network Perspective
creator: T Sentell, K Saiki, M A Abrams, A Jones, K Melendez, J Chevrolet, M Roman, J Barnes, E Patterson
description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic underscored the vital importance of health literacy to combat misinformation, increase trust, and ensure health equity. Health literacy is a collective responsibility, including for organizations to “equitably enable individuals to find, understand, and use information and services.” This presentation will share key insights concerning health literacy in a social context.

title: Hyperspectral imaging meets 3D Gaussian Splatting: A novel approach beyond 3D plant morphology
creator: Wenzhe Deng, Tingting Wu, Zhichao Ni, Yajie Liu, Hanyue Jia, Qingping Ling
description: Accurate acquisition of plant phenotypes is crucial for elucidating plant growth and development, underlying genetic mechanisms, and responses to environmental stimuli. Traditional three-dimensional (3D) phenotyping mainly captures geometric traits such as height, leaf area, and canopy volume, while overlooking physiological and biochemical information.

title: Embracing public health approaches to gambling? A review of global legislative and regulatory trends
creator: D Ukhova, V Marionneau, J Nikkinen, H Wardle
description: Background/IssueThe public health community has increasingly called for governments to recognise the health harms associated with gambling, and for prevention policies to include population-based approaches. Whether and to what extent these calls have translated into actual policy-making globally has not been investigated. Our paper fills this gap.

title: An assessment of US dairy industry needs for digital tools in food safety and quality management
creator: Jun Su, Martin Wiedmann
description: Graphical AbstractSummary:Adoption of digital tools for food safety and quality in the US dairy industry is uneven. Larger companies often have advanced digital systems and increasingly use tools for predictive insights and operational optimization, whereas smaller firms are reported to largely remain reliant on manual, paper-based processes.

title: Toward Explainable Carcinogenicity Prediction: An Integrated Cheminformatics Approach and Consensus Framework for Possibly Carcinogenic Chemicals
creator: Huynh Anh Duy, Tarapong Srisongkram
description: A carcinogenicity assessment of possibly carcinogenic chemicals (International Agency for Research on Cancer: IARC class 2B) was conducted using a consensus framework constructed from three complementary machine learning models: BiLSTM with MACCS fingerprints, LightGBM with RDKit descriptors, and Random Forest (RF) with E-state features.

title: Roadmap for implementation of genomics in healthcare: towards equity in access to genomics
creator: F Lopes, A Costa, M L Cardoso, I Custers, A Merchant, M Konopko, S Scollen, A Vicente
description: IssueImplementing genomic medicine in healthcare can bring us closer to making personalised medicine a reality, with notable socioeconomic benefits.Description of the problemThe 1+Million Genomes Initiative is promoting a reflection in European countries regarding their national strategies for genomic medicine, and how these contribute to research and improve clinical practice.

title: 10.B. Workshop: Combatting AMR: European collaboration to ensure sustained access to effective antibiotics
creator: Organised by: European Observatory on Health Systems and Policies, Chair persons: Dimitra Panteli (Belgium), Elias Mossialos (UK)
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is one of the greatest public health threats facing the world today. The health and economic impacts of AMR are a major challenge for all healthcare systems and societies worldwide. It is estimated that antibiotic-resistant infections are responsible for a substantial number of deaths in Europe each year, with a health burden comparable to that of influenza, tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS combined and a cost of about €1.1 billion to the healthcare systems of EU/EEA countries.

title: Do We Need to Monitor B‐Vitamins and Homocysteine During Initiation of Foslevodopa/Foscarbidopa Therapy?
creator: Aida Shaghaghi‐Zadeh, Matthias Höllerhage, Florian Wegner, Lan Ye, Ishana Schneidereit, Tobias Hegelmaier, Rebecca Jacob, Christoph Schrader, Martin Klietz
description: vodopa (l‐dopa) prodrug, its administration is directly linked to l‐dopa metabolism. 3 In patients receiving l‐dopa therapy, including oral l‐dopa/carbidopa and l‐dopa/carbidopa intestinal gel, alterations in B‐vitamin metabolism and homocysteine levels have been reported. 4 However, data on short‐term changes in B‐vitamin and homocysteine levels during initiation of foslevodopa/foscarbidopa infusion therapy remain limited.

title: Beta-Glucan modulates monocyte plasticity and differentiation capacity to mitigate DSS-induced colitis
creator: Yinyin Lv, Yanyun Fan, Qingxiang Gao, Qiongyun Chen, Yiqun Hu, Lin Wang, Huaxiu Shi, Ermei Chen, Qinyu Xu, Ying Cai, Qingqi Fan, Linying Li, Dan Du, Jianlin Ren, Shih-Chin Cheng, Hongzhi Xu, Boris Novakovic, Yinyin Lv, Yanyun Fan, Qingxiang Gao, Qiongyun Chen, Yiqun Hu, Lin Wang, Huaxiu Shi, Ermei C
description: Trained immunity involves the reprogramming of innate immune cells after an initial exposure, resulting in heightened inflammatory responses to subsequent stimuli and enhanced bactericidal capacity during infection. However, this pro-inflammatory state could also exacerbate chronic conditions like inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), which is characterized by persistent inflammation and microbial imbalance.

title: Asymmetric niche partitioning in large omnivores in response to anthropogenic disturbances within subarctic ecosystems
creator: Ludovick Brown, Chrystal Mantyka‐Pringle, Joël Potié, Pascale Savage, Megan Hornseth, Jason T. Fisher
description: Niche partitioning is an evolutionary process that allows the coexistence of multiple species in a landscape. However, human disturbance can interfere with this process. For instance, humans may displace competitors and favour species with a greater tolerance for disturbances. American black bears (Ursus americanus) and grizzly bears (U.

title: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia Unveils Its Dark Side: A Rare Case of Megakaryocytic Blast Crisis
creator: Mehreen Khalid, Maymoona Suhail, Alizah Faisal, FNU Poombal, Fatima Muhammad Asad Khan
description: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) can progress from a chronic phase (CP) to an accelerated phase (AP) or an acute leukemia-like blastic phase (BP). However, transformation into a megakaryoblastic phase is very rare, and such a progression is clinically significant due to its poor prognosis and resistance to standard tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs).

title: Clinical manifestations and ultrasonographic features of lobular endocervical glandular hyperplasia: a retrospective study of 135 patients
creator: Xiuying Chen, Zhiyun Xue, Sulan Zhao, Li Sun, Bin Li
description: BackgroundLobular endocervical glandular hyperplasia (LEGH) is a precursor to malignant lesions of the endocervix. However, precise histopathological sampling for early detection remains a challenge. This study aimed to review the clinical features of LEGH and particularly focus on its ultrasonographic characteristics.PatientsA retrospective analysis was conducted on 135 patients with LEGH (including those with or without concurrent malignancy).

title: Resolution of Molluscum Contagiosum After Discontinuation of Topical Corticosteroids During Dupilumab Therapy for Atopic Dermatitis: A Case Report
creator: Marina Yunoki, Kensuke Fukuchi, Toshiharu Fujiyama, Taisuke Ito, Tetsuya Honda
description: A 35-year-old male patient with atopic dermatitis (AD) was referred to our department for exacerbated AD lesions. His sudden discontinuation of topical corticosteroid had induced erythroderma on his face, extremities, and trunk. Additionally, he presented small multiple whitish papules, mainly on the trunk and thighs, diagnosed as molluscum contagiosum (MC). Dupilumab was initiated in combination with a topical corticosteroid (0.

title: Programs for responding after patients are harmed by their healthcare: A Making Healthcare Safer IV rapid review
creator: Lauge Sokol-Hessner, C Matthew Stewart, Ritu Sharma, Allen Zhang, Thomas H Gallagher, Allen Kachalia, Eric B Bass, Marisa Clifton
description: BackgroundPatient harm from healthcare is prevalent, serious, and can be long lasting. How healthcare organizations respond has implications for patients, families, healthcare professionals, and organizations. We sought to synthesize the evidence on the effectiveness of communication and resolution programs (CRPs).

title: Juvenile Mice Develop Infarct-Induced Neurodegeneration and Emerging Cognitive Decline in a Model of Pediatric Stroke
creator: Elizabeth W. Mayne, Kelly A. Vanden, Meghan E. Hefferon, Kristy A. Zera, Marion S. Buckwalter
description: BACKGROUND:Over half of pediatric stroke survivors have permanent cognitive deficits, which can emerge late after stroke. Mechanisms of cognitive decline after pediatric stroke may differ from those in adults because children’s strokes occur while brain and immune development are still ongoing.

title: Free School Meals Extension to all 4-11 year olds in primary education in Wales
creator: L Green, C Emmerson
description: There were 272,339 primary age students in Wales in April 2021, of whom 63,614 (23%) were entitled to free school meals. Free school meals (FSMs) are currently means tested in Wales. Estimates suggest around 40,000 children in primary education may be currently living in poverty but are not eligible for a free school meal .

title: An evaluation of designs for Phase I/IIa dose-finding studies in Tuberculosis
creator: Alessandra Serra, Pavel Mozgunov, Patrick PJ Phillips, Thomas Jaki
description: Early development of tuberculosis (TB) treatments often separates dose-finding in healthy volunteers (Phase I) and safety and early activity in patients (Phase IIa). The BTZ-043 study (NCT04044001) is a recent study that combined these two objectives in patients in a single study.

title: Successes, lessons learned and recommendations for the future: Experiences from the first year of Ontario’s nirsevimab program for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prophylaxis in infants
creator: Bosco Paes, Erin Fleischer, Jane Healey, Eddy Lau, Graeme N. Smith
description: At the conclusion of the 2024/2025 respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) season in Ontario, a panel of healthcare providers who were actively involved in the conduct of the province’s first RSV prophylaxis program with nirsevimab in infants, assembled to discuss their experiences.

title: How do health authorities inform about general practitioner selection? Analysis of Italian Websites
creator: A Vinci, L Pirrotta, M Vainieri
description: BackgroundThe Next Generation EU and Italian Recovery and Resilience Plan share the common goal of supporting digital transformation. In health, adequate digitalization and web communication strategies are essential to achieve adequate population health outcomes. This work describes the level of digitalization and information of a fundamental primary care service: the choice or change of the General Practitioner (GP).

title: Differences in intestinal microbiota in Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder
creator: Alba Troci, Julienne Haas, Anna Weiß, Sebastian Heinzel, Andre Franke, Daniela Berg, Corinna Bang, Eva Schaeffer
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Previous studies have shown differences in the microbiota of patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) compared to healthy controls (HC). To deduce a possible causality, it is highly relevant to examine changes in the prodromal phase.

title: Analysing public debates, to support productive engagement with politicians and stakeholders
creator: S Sinclair
description: IssueUK public health debates have become highly politicised. Sean Sinclair (SCS) conducted 37 semi-structured interviews with public health professionals to understand how this affects their engagement with stakeholders. Interviewees said it has become more difficult to gain stakeholder support for public health policies. They hypothesised that politicians didn’t listen to evidence regarding health outcomes.

title: Evaluation of the Phytochemical Composition, Antioxidant Activity, and Enzyme Inhibitory Potential of Salvia heldreichiana Within the Framework of Molecular Docking and CAVER Tunnel Analysis
creator: Erdi Can Aytar, Esin Çolak, Kaan Bedirhan Kahveci, Abidin Gümrükçüoğlu, Süleyman Doğu, Betül Aydın
description: Medicinal plants are widely used in traditional medicine, and Salvia species hold an important place in Turkish folk medicine. This study comprehensively evaluated the phytochemical composition, antioxidant potential, enzyme inhibitory activity, molecular docking, and CAVER tunnel properties of Salvia heldreichiana. HPLC analysis identified 4‐hydroxybenzoic acid, rosmarinic acid, p‐coumaric acid, and chrysin as the major bioactive constituents.

title: Role of immune cell subsets in liver fibrosis through single-cell RNA sequencing and array
creator: Bo Yang, Junjie Yuan, Jingwen Zhao, Xin Chen
description: BackgroundImmune-inflammatory responses and dysregulation play a key role in liver fibrosis (LF) and cirrhosis progression, but the phenotypic and functional dynamics of immune cell populations remain poorly characterized.MethodsLF-related data from the GEO database were analyzed using ssGSEA to quantify immune cell infiltration and Kaplan-Meier analysis to assess the prognostic value of specific immune cell populations.

title: Why is the muscle spindle so complicated?
creator: Vaughan G Macefield
description: ings from single afferents of muscle spindle primary endings by Adrian and Zotterman was published in 1926), yet its operation continues to yield surprises. As the only mechanoreceptor in the somatosensory nervous system with its own motor supply [the fusimotor (gamma) motoneurones, which regulate the sensitivity of the primary and secondary endings to stretch], it truly is a wonderful beast.

title: M2 Macrophages are Major Mediators of Germline Risk of Endometriosis and Explain Pleiotropy With Comorbid Traits
creator: Soledad Ochoa, Fernanda S Rasquel‐Oliveira, Brett McKinnon, Marcela Haro, Sugarniya Subramaniam, Pak Yu, Simon Coetzee, Michael S Anglesio, Kelly N Wright, Raanan Meyer, Anne E Porter, Caroline E Gargett, Sally Mortlock, Grant W Montgomery, Michael S Rogers, Kate Lawrenson
description: Endometriosis is a common gynecologic condition that causes chronic, life‐altering symptoms including pain and infertility. There is an urgent need for new non‐hormonal targeted therapeutics to treat endometriosis, but until very recently, the cellular and molecular signatures of endometriotic lesions are undefined, hindering the development of clinical advances.

title: Assessing calcification effects in TEVAR procedures: a computational analysis
creator: Giulia De Campo, Anna Ramella, Sara Barati, Giulia Luraghi, Virginia Fregona, Maurizio Domanin, Robin Heijmen, Santi Trimarchi, Francesco Migliavacca
description: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) procedure is sometimes discouraged from clinical guidelines in the presence of calcifications and thrombus along the sealing zones. This computational study aims to understand which is the effect of calcification on stent graft displacement after TEVAR procedure, simulated in a patient-specific anatomy with a penetrating aortic ulcer (PAU).

title: Rare autosomal recessive hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type VI in a Pakistani family caused by a novel DST variant
creator: Riaz Ahmad, Mina Zamani, Muhammad Naeem, Henry Houlden
description: BackgroundHereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathies (HSANs) are rare inherited disorders characterized by sensory and autonomic nerve dysfunction classified into eight subtypes. HSAN-VI (OMIM: 614653) is an autosomal recessive subtype which manifests severe pain insensitivity, neonatal hypotonia, respiratory and feeding difficulties, lack of psychomotor development and autonomic abnormalities.

title: Myeloid cell renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system in hypertension and inflammation
creator: Claude F Albritton, Sepiso K Masenga, Andrea Marshall, Antentor Hinton, Annet Kirabo
description: This review explores the intersection of the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system (RAAS) and myeloid cell biology, with particular focus on how their interaction contributes to hypertension pathogenesis and related inflammatory comorbidities. While the classical RAAS is well-established in systemic blood pressure control and fluid balance, evidence is mounting that immune cells possess an intrinsic RAAS that influences inflammatory processes.

title: A Case of Liver Injury Immediately After Initiation of Triple Therapy in a Patient With BRAF V600E Mutation-Positive Colorectal Cancer
creator: Yuka Aimono, Atsushi Ohkawara, Tatsunori Ogawa, Takahiro Yagisawa, Akihiro Tamura
description: The combination therapy of binimetinib, encorafenib, and cetuximab ("triplet regimen") was approved in Japan in November 2020 for the second-line treatment of BRAF V600E mutation-positive colorectal cancer. In this study, we encountered a patient who developed a liver injury requiring drug withdrawal on day eight of the triplet regimen administration.

title: Quality of Life Assessment Using the Leg Activity Measure in Ambulatory Individuals With Leg Spasticity: Findings From a Longitudinal, Observational Study Evaluating the Effectiveness of AbobotulinumtoxinA in Routine Practice
creator: Stephen Ashford, Alberto Esquenazi, Richard D. Zorowitz, Mathieu Beneteau, Pascal Maisonobe, Christian Hannes, Jorge Jacinto, AboLiSh Study group
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the effect of repeat abobotulinumtoxinA treatment on quality of life (QOL) in patients with leg spasticity.DesignSecondary analysis of the prospective, longitudinal (16mo), observational AboLiSh study.SettingSpecialist neurorehabilitation centers across 9 countries.ParticipantsAmbulatory adults (66.4% men, mean age 53.9y) with unilateral lower limb spasticity able to take ≥5 steps with or without assistance.

title: Two-Dimensional MXene-Based Advanced Sensors for Neuromorphic Computing Intelligent Application
creator: Lin Lu, Bo Sun, Zheng Wang, Jialin Meng, Tianyu Wang
description: Highlights The latest research progress in the field of MXene-based neuromorphic computing is reviewed.The design strategy of MXene-based neuromorphic devices encompasses multiple factors are summarized, including material selection, circuit integration, and architecture optimization.Future development paths for MXene-based neuromorphic computing are discussed, including large-scale manufacturing, stability enhancement, and interdisciplinary integration.

title: Jailing of transvenous leads during transcutaneous tricuspid valve replacement: A perilous future?
creator: Jeffrey Kolominsky, Frank Bogun, Mohammed Saeed, Amrish Deshmukh
description: te atrioventricular (AV) block within 30 days of implantation. •Jailing preexisting transvenous leads can cause subacute lead compromise, which may not be detected on standard device interrogation. Jailing preexisting transvenous leads can cause subacute lead compromise, which may not be detected on standard device interrogation.

title: Exploring Motivating Factors for Pursuing Radiation Oncology: A Comparative Analysis of Medical Students and Residents
creator: Brandon S Chai, Maryam Dosani, Timothy Kong, Paris-Ann Ingledew
description: PurposeIncreasing medical student (MS) interest in radiation oncology (RO) is important to meet the rising demand for radiation oncologists. Understanding the factors that drive MS to pursue RO is crucial. This study compares motivating factors between MS and RO residents to inform interventions to increase recruitment and sustained interest in the specialty.

title: Evaluation of Cardiac IL-11 and IL-11Rα Expression During T. cruzi Infection
creator: Yarlla Loyane Lira Braga, José Rodrigues do Carmo Neto, Pablo Igor Ribeiro Franco, Jordana Fernandes de Oliveira, Rafael Obata Trevisan, Fernanda Bernadelli de Vito, Flávia Aparecida de Oliveira, Mara Rúbia Nunes Celes, Marcos Vinícius da Silva, Juliana Reis Machado
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Chagas disease (CD), caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, leads to cardiomyopathy in approximately 20–30% of infected individuals. Interleukin-11 (IL-11) has been implicated in cardiac fibrosis, although its immunological role in this context remains unclear. This study investigated the temporal dynamics of IL-11 and its receptor, IL-11Rα, expression in the hearts of C57BL/6 mice infected with 1,000 trypomastigote forms of the Y or Colombian strains of T. Mice were euthanized at 5, 15, 30, 60, and 120 days post-infection (dpi).

title: RNA processing kinase inhibitors and epigenetic inhibitors in combination with oncology drugs or investigational agents in multi-cell type patient-derived tumor cell line spheroids
creator: Beverly A. Teicher, Thomas S. Dexheimer, Thomas Silvers, Nathan P. Coussens, Eric Jones, Steven D. Gore, Mark Kunkel, James H. Doroshow
description: PurposeThe alternative splicing of mRNA precursors allows one gene to yield multiple proteins with distinct functions. CDC-like kinases serve as pivotal regulators of alternative splicing. Control of protein expression also occurs at the level of DNA through histone methylation and demethylation.

title: Effect of Comprehensive Balance Modulating Strategies on Physical Performance Among the Elderly in Care Home Settings in Southern India
creator: Binoy Mathew K. V., Jagatheesan Alagesan, Prathap Suganthirababu
description: PurposeGlobally, the proportion of the elderly population is rising. Age-related physical performance impairments are more common and affect quality of life. This study aimed to investigate the impact of a new exercise regimen called Comprehensive Balance-Modulating Strategies (CBMS) on the physical performance of older adults living in care home settings.

title: Real‐world‐data for phenotypes and genotypes of rare monogenic genetic epilepsies and genes of uncertain significance for epilepsy
creator: Haley Morris, Elizabeth Mathew, Shalini Bahl, Marta Villa‐Lopez, Saadet Mercimek‐Andrews
description: ObjectivesThe objectives of this study were to develop a real‐world‐data (RWD) database for patients with epilepsy to provide further real‐world‐evidence (RWE) for monogenic genetic epilepsies; to assess the usefulness of a diagnostic algorithm in epilepsy; and to examine protein 3D structures using in silico tools to predict variant pathogenicity.

title: Competency framework on simulation model-based decision-making for Master of Public Health students
creator: R Hrzic, M V Cade, BLH Wong, N McCreesh, J Simon, K Czabanowska
description: BackgroundSimulation models support decision-making by helping public health practitioners evaluate the potential effects of interventions in complex systems and their ultimate health impacts. However, many public health professionals remain unfamiliar with constructing simulation models and how best to use their outputs for decision-making due to a lack of training.

title: Double-Bond Character of Phosphates in Solid and Liquid Phases Probed by Oxygen K‑Edge X‑ray Absorption Spectroscopy
creator: Masanari Nagasaka, Fumitoshi Kumaki, Jun-ichi Adachi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Double-bond character of phosphate groups has important roles for biological reactions and was investigated using the PO π* peaks in the oxygen K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS). The O K-edge XAS spectra of phosphates in the solid phase found that the double-bond character of phosphates is enhanced as the negative charge increases, where the weak PO π* peak was observed in NaH2PO4, but distinct PO π* peaks were obtained in Na2HPO4 and Na3PO4.

title: The mental health of children and adolescents at Matosinhos: characteristics and obstacles to care
creator: R Barbabela, G Duarte, T Leão
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundMental health disorders are a public health issue. Most mental disorders begin during childhood and adolescence. Epidemiological studies regarding the diagnosis, prevalence, and access to treatment by children and adolescents are scarce, especially in Portugal.

title: Low-Temperature Electrolytes for Lithium-Ion Batteries: Current Challenges, Development, and Perspectives
creator: Yang Zhao, Limin Geng, Weijia Meng, Jiaye Ye
description: Highlights Key electrolyte-related factors limiting the low-temperature performance of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are analyzed.Emerging strategies to enhance the low-temperature performance of LIBs are summarized from the perspectives of electrolyte engineering and artificial intelligence (AI) -assisted design.Perspectives and challenges on AI-driven design, advanced characterization, and novel electrolyte systems for low-temperature LIBs.

title: Illuminating a joyless life: qualitative, transdiagnostic exploration of anhedonia
creator: Clementine J. Edwards, Chloe Osei-Cobbina, Alison Duerden, Nicola Sirey, Vidhi Bassi, Adeola Agunbiade, Matteo Cella, Barnaby D. Dunn, Andrew Gumley
description: BackgroundAnhedonia (loss of pleasure) is a core feature of both depression and psychosis and yet the experience is not well understood. This limits our ability to effectively target it with psychological or pharmacological interventions.AimsThe aim of this study was to explore the experience of anhedonia, for the first time from a transdiagnostic perspective.

title: Quasi-experimental evaluations of health-related policies in Europe: a scoping review
creator: K Sell, S Rabbani, J Burns
description: BackgroundQuasi-experimental methods (QEM) are study designs increasingly used in public health to evaluate the impact of health-focused policies. We sought to examine the scope, methodological characteristics as well as health equity considerations of policy evaluations using QEM that assess health and social outcomes in Europe.MethodsWe conducted a scoping review as outlined in our pre-registered protocol (https://osf.io/n5rvg).

title: Aspirin or non‐steroidal anti‐inflammatory drug initiation and subsequent bladder cancer evaluation
creator: Malene Söth Hansen, Lars Dyrskjøt, Uffe Heide‐Jørgensen, Jørgen Bjerggaard Jensen, Mette Nørgaard
description: BackgroundWhether aspirin or non‐aspirin non‐steroidal anti‐inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) initiation may unmask unknown bladder cancers (BCs) by hematuria remains controversial.ObjectivesTo evaluate unmasking, we compared cystoscopy rates, BC prevalence at cystoscopy, and invasive stage prevalence at diagnosis in aspirin or NSAID initiators with never‐users.

title: Policy developments on labelling for a more sustainable food system
creator: N Gokani
description: Governments across Europe are developing policies which promote healthier, more sustainable food choices. This presentation explores these policies with a focus on the EU. In May 2020, the European Commission published its Farm to Fork Strategy which acknowledged the inextricable links between healthy people, healthy societies and a healthy planet.

title: Efficient Direct Recycling of Spent Batteries: Integrated Lithiation and Delamination
creator: Jeonghwan Song, Seok Hyun Song, Dokyeong Han, Jaehyun Noh, Jayoung Kim, Min Jeong Kim, Hayong Song, Jeong‐Sun Park, Jaekook Kim, Jiyoung Ma, Jinju Song, Jung‐Je Woo
description: Direct recycling offers a promising alternative for regenerating spent Li‐ion batteries (LIBs); however, achieving high‐purity cathode and ensuring cost‐effectiveness remains challenging. Herein, we present an innovative integrated process that simultaneously enables delamination and relithiation of spent cathodes, LixNi0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O2 and LixFePO4, under open‐air conditions with minimal energy.

title: Future-self vividness influences acceptance of camera-based active and assisted living technologies
creator: N Tham, A-M Brady, J Dinsmore
description: BackgroundCamera-based active and assisted living (AAL) technologies are an eminent solution to the accruing burdens of population ageing but are hardly accepted by older adults. The technology's privacy implications and perceived usefulness are established antecedents to its acceptance. However, one understudied barrier to acceptance is a failure in future self-identification.

title: Evaluation of family physicians’ attitude towards primary healthcare consultations
creator: V Jasiukaitiene, I Venckute
description: BackgroundThe quality of services in the health care system is very important for both patients’ health and health care providers. In the past decade, good service ratings from the patient's perspective have become crucial in evaluating the work of medical professionals and health care institutions.

title: A Rare Case of Gastric Trichobezoar Managed by Laparotomy
creator: Aneesh Rao Nadipelli, Dileep Duggineni
description: Trichobezoars, rare gastrointestinal foreign bodies composed of ingested hair, typically affect females with psychiatric disorders such as trichotillomania and pica. This case report highlights the diagnostic and treatment challenges in an 18-year-old female presenting with a left upper quadrant mass and pain, who was found to have a large gastric trichobezoar.

title: Treatment of Pathological Proximal Femur Fracture in a Child With a Unicameral Bone Cyst: A Case Report
creator: Philip Lew Wei Sheng, Ahmad Fazly Abd Rasid, Kamal Jamil
description: Pathological proximal femur fractures secondary to unicameral bone cysts in the pediatric age group are uncommon. Despite the development of modern surgical treatments and implant choices, it is still debatable what the gold standard of treatment is for a unicameral bone cyst with pathological proximal femur fractures.

title: The impact of digital health literacy on anxiety and preventive behaviors during the pandemic
creator: M Duplaga, M Wojcieszko
description: BackgroundFrom the pandemic's beginning, many authors suggested that digital health literacy (DHL) may be an important factor in protecting against araising misinformation and enhancing compliance with preventive behaviors. In this study, we analyzed the effect of DHL on future anxiety and generalized anxiety, as well as on adherence to preventive measures and COVID-19 vaccination uptake after adjusting for sociodemographic factors.

title: An extensive morphological and molecular characterization of the neglected class Odontostomatea (Ciliophora)
creator: Daniel Méndez-Sánchez, Ondřej Pomahač, Marek Valt, William A Bourland, Ivan Čepička
description: Odontostomatid ciliates, known for over a century, were historically classified within various taxonomic groups of Ciliophora Doflein, 1901 until their reclassification into the class Odontostomatea. Despite the recognition of 25 valid species, most descriptions predate the advent of silver impregnation and sequencing methods.

title: Developing tailor-made plant-based dishes with adolescents for school canteens
creator: M Kokkorou, C Dinnella, S Spinelli, J Wollgast, P Maragkoudakis, E Monteleone
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). School interventions can have a significant impact on promoting plant-based (PB) diets, which can benefit both health and environmental sustainability. This co-creation and repeated exposure study was conducted in a high school and is divided into 3 parts, a) Co-creation with adolescents (aged 12-16) and chefs to develop innovative PB dishes, b) Global profile (liking, sensory properties, emotions) of the new dishes, c) Repeated exposure for 6 weeks.

title: Coping and family functionality in women with diabetes and breast cancer
creator: María Valeria Jiménez-Báez, Sofía Concepción Thomas-Gómez, Gabriel González-Guerrero, David Rojano-Mejía, Eduardo Patricio Achurra-Godinez
description: IntroductionBreast cancer (BC) is the second leading cause of death in Mexican women. Comorbidity with type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) is a risk factor for complications.ObjectiveTo evaluate the evolution of family functionality and coping in patients with BC and T2DM after 4 years of diagnosis.MethodLongitudinal cohort study in women with BC and T2DM in Quintana Roo.

title: Asthma prevalence and environmental exposure in children and adolescent in Slovenia – a pilot study
creator: T Rejc, A Kukec, A Mlakar, T Carli, U Krivec, A Zver
description: BackgroundThe last data on asthma prevalence (13.9 and 17.4%) in children in Slovenia is from 2002. The aim is to assess the asthma prevalence and environmental risk factors in two selected schools in Slovenia, as a pilot study for a national cross-sectional survey.MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional pilot study in two primary schools in Slovenia.

title: Dramatic Remodeling of Hypoplastic Pulmonary Arteries by Pulmonary Valve Opening, Right Ventricular Outflow Stenting, and Aortopulmonary Collateral Lung Territory Incorporation
creator: Marjan Hesari, Derek Van, Srujan Ganta, Justin Ryan, Jessica Haley, Jose Silva Sepulveda, Rohit Rao, Brent Gordon, John Nigro, Howaida G El-Said
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPulmonary atresia with severely hypoplastic pulmonary arteries (PAHP), with or without major aortopulmonary collateral arteries (MAPCA), is a significant clinical conundrum. This case series aims to present a strategy being evaluated for patients with PAHP, highlighting the effectiveness of pulmonary valve opening, right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) stenting, and staged serial interventions in promoting pulmonary artery (PA) growth and improving PA architecture.

title: Promoting healthy learning: A participatory health promotion project with healthcare students
creator: T Schloemer, L Domenik, A-C Dreyer, L Scheu
description: BackgroundHealth promotion is of great importance during education to prepare future health professionals for their work. Students need to cope with long periods of sitting, stress and high workload through practical training in the healthcare sector. Based on students’ experiences, we developed a project to promote healthy learning at a University of applied Sciences for Health in Germany.

title: Interventional Management of Intracardiac Masses
creator: Pedro Engel Gonzalez, James A. Goldstein
description: successful relief of thrombi in transit, vegetations on the tricuspid valve and electrophysiologic leads, and even tumors, thereby reducing the risk of problematic pulmonary embolic events. Left-sided intracardiac masses pose far greater clinical risk attributable to the potentially catastrophic nature of systemic cardioembolic events, particularly major ischemic stroke.

title: Visceral obesity as a predictor of ileal pouch reachability in ulcerative colitis: A prospective single-center study
creator: Yuki Horio, Motoi Uchino, Masato Kiriki, Yusuke Tomoo, Kazunori Nomura, Kentaro Nagano, Kurando Kusunoki, Ryuichi Kuwahara, Kei Kimura, Kozo Kataoka, Masataka Ikeda, Hiroki Ikeuchi
description: AimObesity has been reported to increase the risk of technical inability in performing ileal pouch–anal anastomosis (IPAA) in patients with ulcerative colitis (UC). This study aimed to prospectively investigate the association between visceral fat and the feasibility of pouch reach in hand-sewn IPAA.MethodsWe prospectively enrolled patients with UC scheduled for two-stage restorative proctocolectomy with a preoperative plan for hand-sewn IPAA.

title: Is fondaparinux safe for use during pregnancy? A state-of-the-art review of current evidence
creator: Yuexiao Wu, Yurou Ji, Siqi Wang, Yayi Hu, Dan Shan
description: Fondaparinux, a synthetic pentasaccharide, represents the smallest heparin-based molecule and functions as a potent selective indirect inhibitor of activated factor Xa. Its high bioavailability, ease of dosing, and favorable tolerability profile render it an ideal antithrombotic agent for pregnant patients who are intolerant to unfractionated heparin (UFH) and low-molecular-weight heparins (LMWHs).

title: eHealth profile of patients with diabetes
creator: M Jendly, V Santschi, S Tancredi, I Konzelmann, L Raboud, Arnaud Chiolero
description: BackgroundDigital health technology can be useful to improve the health of patients with diabetes, to support patient-centered care, and self-management. In this cross-sectional study, we described the eHealth profile of patients with diabetes, based on their use of digital health technology, and its association with sociodemographic characteristics.

title: Histamine regulates the activity and the expression of the Na+/H+ exchanger (NHE)3 in human epithelial HK-2 cells
creator: Chiara Gerbino, Federica Foglietta, Daniele Corsi, Patrizia Nardini, Luigi Cangemi, Elisa Benetti, Arianna Carolina Rosa
description: Objective and designInvestigate the potential role of histamine and its receptors on the functional expression of the sodium/hydrogen (Na+/H+) exchanger (NHE)3.MaterialThe human epithelial kidney (HK-2) cells were used as an in vitro model of the renal proximal tubule.TreatmentHK-2 cells were exposed to histamine 0–1000 nM alone or in combination with chlorphenamine (10 μM) and JNJ-7777120 (1 μM) for 0–48 h.

title: Spatially Resolved ABA Signalling Reveals Dual Role in Tomato Yield
creator: Fu‐An Wen, Fu‐Dong Mai, Ji‐Bin Xiao, Hong Zhang, Xuan Zhou, Xin‐Yu Yang, Yelena Sterlin, David Karpovsky, Ke‐Ting Li, Juan Wang, Jia Liu, Shi‐Hao Su, Assaf Mosquna, Yu‐Fei Sun
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Abscisic acid (ABA) is a central hormonal regulator of plant adaptation to stress and developmental progression. However, its contribution to agronomic traits such as yield remains unclear due to the pleiotropic nature of ABA signalling. To disentangle distinct physiological functions of ABA, we employed a receptor‐specific gain‐of‐function strategy in tomato, activating downstream signalling independently of endogenous hormone levels in an ABA‐deficient background.

title: Health literacy and unhealthy lifestyle behaviors in older adults: does social connectedness matter?
creator: M Wieczorek, C Meier, M Kliegel, J Maurer
description: BackgroundGiven the high prevalence of low health literacy (HL), the lifestyle-related morbidity, and the importance of the social environment in later life, we aimed to investigate the association between HL and unhealthy lifestyle behaviors and explore the moderating role of social connectedness in this relationship in a population-based sample of adults aged 58+.

title: Chondroitin sulfate restores muscle mass via gut–muscle axis remodeling through sugar–bile acid metabolism reprogramming
creator: Ruiyun Wu, Tao Wen, Nan Shang, Penghao Xie, Zhenyu Wang, Hang Li, Shaobo Li, Dequan Zhang
description: Glucocorticoid‐induced myopathy is characterized by progressive muscle atrophy and impaired regeneration, yet effective microbiota‐oriented interventions for preserving muscle homeostasis remain largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that dietary chondroitin sulfate (DCS) restores muscle mass and function through a microbiota‐dependent gut–muscle metabolic axis. DCS failed to confer protection in germ‐free or antibiotic‐treated mice, establishing gut microbiota as a prerequisite for its efficacy.

title: Introducing outdoor office work to reduce stress among office workers in Sweden
creator: F Javan Abraham, P Andreasson, A King, K Bälter, S Toivanen
description: BackgroundOffice workplace stress is concerning as it leads to adverse and chronic health outcomes. Outdoor office work (OOW), an innovative practice may address these challenges as being outdoors has potential benefits. This study aims to assess stress among office workers that are working in their normal indoor office compared to practicing OOW and identifying facilitators and barriers for doing OOW.

title: Burkholderia pseudomallei PenI β-lactamase and variants are potently inhibited by taniborbactam
creator: Maria F. Mojica, Scott A. Becka, Mitchell Edwards, Cullen Myers, Kyoko Uehara, Tsuyoshi Uehara, Tyuji Hoshino, Elise T. Zeiser, Cassandra L. Chatwin, David A. Six, Robert A. Bonomo, Krisztina M. Papp-Wallace, Michiyoshi Nukaga
description: Burkholderia pseudomallei is a Gram-negative pathogen that causes melioidosis, a severe and often fatal disease. Due to its recognized potential as a bioterrorism agent, it is critical that appropriate antimicrobial agents are available for post-exposure prophylaxis and treatment of melioidosis.

title: Pharmacogenomic profiling of the efficacy of gemcitabine monotherapy in metastatic pancreatic cancer: Subgroup analysis of the GENESECT study
creator: Takashi Yokokawa, Daiki Tsuji, Masahiro Hatori, Kazuyoshi Kawakami, Masahiko Nakao, Takuya Yano, Yuichiro Arakawa, Keisuke Matsuo, Yasukata Ohashi, Masato Ozaka, Naoki Sasahira, Yasuhiko Sakata, Yuki Kogure, Shinya Tamaki, Atsushi Wada, Yusuke Taki, Wataru Suzuki, Kazuo Kobayashi, Hiroshi Ishii, Kun
description: AimIn the GENESECT study, no significant gemcitabine (GEM) metabolism‐related germline genetic polymorphisms (GPs) were identified because approximately 70% of patients received combination therapy with nab‐paclitaxel, which has metabolic pathways different from GEM. title: 线粒体融合、分裂和自噬在烧伤创面愈合中的作用研究进展
creator: 泽浩 李, 伟雪 金, 松雪 郭
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 线粒体作为细胞内的“能量工厂”，其功能和结构的稳定性对于创面愈合极为重要。烧伤后，线粒体损伤会放大炎症反应、启动内源性凋亡通路、导致三磷酸腺苷合成不足，从而延缓修复。线粒体融合、分裂的动态平衡及线粒体自噬过程是调控线粒体结构完整性和功能稳定性的关键途径。线粒体通过融合与分裂动态平衡及线粒体自噬保护烧伤创面：适度线粒体分裂可促进创面愈合，过度分裂则引发过量活性氧及炎症因子产生而不利于修复，线粒体融合对创面愈合可能具有益处；线粒体自噬可减轻细胞凋亡和氧化应激，调控烧伤创面愈合各阶段。本文聚焦线粒体融合与分裂平衡维持和线粒体自噬，阐述其在烧伤创面修复中的作用，并探讨这些机制在烧伤后损伤防治中的临床应用前景。

世界卫生组织报告指出，全球每年约有18万人死于烧伤相关原因，烧伤伤害是全球第四大常见伤害类型［1］。烧伤创面愈合进程缓慢且愈合难度较高，不仅给患者带来身心双重痛苦，也对社会医疗资源造成沉重负担。近年来陆续有文献报道烧伤创面损伤进展与线粒体结构破坏及功能损伤相关［2-5］。线粒体作为高度动态的细胞器，是维持细胞代谢、应激反应及内环境稳态的核心结构。作为细胞代谢的中枢枢纽，线粒体调控ATP合成、脂肪酸代谢、活性氧生成、氧化磷酸化、细胞产热及钙稳态等多项关键生化过程［6］。烧伤发生后，这一“能量工厂”会经历结构损伤、功能紊乱和适应性重塑等一系列复杂动态变化，而这些改变正是介导烧伤后细胞凋亡、炎症反应、组织损伤和修复的核心机制。在此过程中，机体可启动线粒体融合、分裂及自噬等修复和重塑机制，从而维持细胞存活并保障其基本功能［7-8］。本文通过阐述线粒体融合、分裂及自噬在缓解烧伤创面损伤中的作用机制，旨在为烧伤创面治疗策略研究提供新思路。

线粒体结构和功能损伤驱动烧伤创面损伤进展

1953年，Jackson医生［9］首次将烧伤创面划分为三个同心圆区域：凝固区、瘀滞区和充血区。瘀滞区因水肿、血管收缩、高凝等病理特点易发生缺血缺氧，进一步导致损伤加重，是烧伤后早期创面进行性加重的关键区域［10］。有研究发现，在烧伤模型皮肤组织中，与线粒体损伤相关基因Nrf-1、CYC1和NDUFA9表达下调，证实了烧伤后存在线粒体损伤［11］。瘀滞区损伤最严重的阶段并非极度缺血时期，而是在48或72 h后血流有所改善时，这可能与线粒体功能损伤相关［12］。线粒体作为对缺氧最为敏感的细胞器，其缺血时电子传递链功能受阻导致活性氧蓄积，待血流改善后进一步加重氧化应激［12］。另有研究显示线粒体损伤与瘀滞区损伤加重过程同步［2］。上述证据共同表明线粒体结构和功能损伤在烧伤创面早期损伤进展中起重要驱动作用。

炎症激活

过度炎症是烧伤创面损伤进展的重要原因，线粒体通过多种途径参与调控炎症反应。烧伤后瘀滞区细胞中线粒体编码DNA与细胞核编码DNA的比率在烧伤后6 h显著下降，这一现象提示烧伤后损伤线粒体中的mtDNA被释放到细胞外［2］。线粒体损伤相关产物可通过多条通路激活炎症反应：一方面，活性氧过量产生、心磷脂外化及mtDNA释放等均可直接激活NLRP3炎症小体，进而加重局部炎症级联反应［13-15］；另一方面，释放的mtDNA可作为cGAS特异性激动剂，启动cGAS-STING1信号通路，进一步放大炎症应答［16］。炎症反应持续激活会导致局部组织过度损伤，同时影响成纤维细胞增殖和胶原蛋白合成，导致瘢痕形成。过度炎症反应也会导致角质形成细胞功能异常，延缓伤口表皮再生，从而增加感染风险［17］。Li等［3］研究发现，在皮肤烧伤模型中，线粒体移植治疗后促炎性细胞因子（如肿瘤坏死因子-α、IL-1β和IL-6）水平降低，而抗炎细胞因子（如IL-10）水平升高，表明结构功能完整的线粒体有利于控制烧伤后炎症反应，且线粒体移植治疗可以有效防止烧伤创面损伤进展。上述研究表明，烧伤后引起的线粒体功能障碍可通过加重组织炎症反应诱导烧伤创面损伤进展，而恢复线粒体功能则可以有效降低炎症反应。

细胞凋亡

细胞凋亡是烧伤创面损伤进展的重要机制，线粒体参与细胞凋亡调控。烧伤后真皮细胞凋亡率明显增加，且细胞凋亡在初次烧伤后至少持续23 d［18］。抑制细胞凋亡可缓解烧伤创面损伤进展，促进伤口愈合［19］。热应激是烧伤后细胞线粒体损伤的关键诱因，线粒体介导的内源性凋亡通路在烧伤创面损伤进展中发挥重要作用。研究显示，热应激会导致角质形成细胞线粒体膜电位下降，破坏细胞膜通透性，同时促进促凋亡蛋白BAK和BAX在角质形成细胞中表达［20］。在烧伤应激的持续作用下，线粒体膜通透性会进一步增加，甚至发生线粒体破裂，导致其正常结构和功能破坏，进而启动内源性凋亡程序：线粒体膜电位丧失、膜通透性增加或线粒体破裂会促使CYC等促凋亡因子释放至细胞质中；释放的CYC可与凋亡蛋白酶激活因子1、Caspase-9结合形成凋亡小体，激活Caspase-3等下游凋亡酶，最终触发细胞凋亡［21-22］。有研究显示，烧伤后CYC、Caspase-3和Caspase-9水平显著上调［2］。Fas/FasL介导的外源性通路作用相对有限，烧伤水疱液中FasL水平无显著升高，提示内源性通路（由线粒体介导）是烧伤后凋亡的主要途径［23］。综上，烧伤诱导的细胞凋亡是驱动创面损伤进展的关键因素，而靶向调控线粒体介导的凋亡通路有望成为改善烧伤创面预后的新策略。

ATP合成不足

线粒体是细胞能量代谢的核心，其通过由复合体Ⅰ~Ⅳ、辅酶Q和CYC构成的电子传递链产生质子梯度，进而在复合体Ⅴ处合成ATP［7］。烧伤后Nrf-1、CYC-1、NDUFA9等基因表达下调［11］。其中，Nrf-1调控氧化磷酸化相关基因表达，CYC-1能够形成复合物维持电子传递链电子流动，NDUFA9是线粒体呼吸链复合体Ⅰ的重要组成部分，这些基因下调会导致电子传递链功能受损、ATP合成减少［11］。研究显示，烧伤后人心肌细胞AC16中AMP活化蛋白激酶、沉默信息调节因子1和PGC-1表达减少，从而阻碍线粒体呼吸能力，减少ATP合成［4］。另外，烧伤后IL-1β表达增加，可刺激一氧化氮生成，从而显著破坏线粒体合成ATP的效率，间接加剧线粒体功能障碍［5］。烧伤创面的愈合过程（包括血小板激活、免疫细胞浸润、胶原蛋白和肉芽组织合成）均离不开ATP，线粒体功能障碍导致ATP合成不足会直接延缓创面修复。

线粒体融合、分裂和自噬在防治烧伤创面损伤中的作用

线粒体融合、分裂和自噬的分子机制

线粒体稳态维持依赖于融合、分裂和自噬构成的动态调控系统，融合维持线粒体群体的均一性，分裂分离受损片段，自噬则彻底清除受损线粒体，三者协同维持线粒体稳态［24-25］。

线粒体融合可分为MFN1/2介导的线粒体外膜融合和OPA1介导的线粒体内膜融合。MFN1/2和OPA1相互协调，共同保证融合发生，其缺乏会导致线粒体形态异常，线粒体融合被阻断［26］。线粒体融合有助于混合和交换线粒体内的成分（包括蛋白质、mtDNA等），维持线粒体的均一性和功能稳定性，并增强氧化磷酸化和ATP生成，对维持线粒体结构完整性（如嵴的完整性、mtDNA维持、呼吸链超复合体组装等）具有重要作用［6，24］。

参与线粒体分裂的关键蛋白包括DRP1、线粒体分裂因子和线粒体分裂蛋白1。受到特定刺激时，DRP1会被线粒体分裂因子和线粒体分裂蛋白1等受体招募到线粒体外膜上，介导线粒体分裂发生［27］。线粒体分裂可以将受损的线粒体部分分离出来，这些受损部分可通过线粒体自噬被清除，从而维持线粒体的整体质量；同时线粒体分裂可将线粒体分割为更易于运输的小型单元，便于其在细胞内灵活移动并精准分布至能量需求旺盛的区域，以高效满足细胞局部的代谢需求［28-29］。

线粒体自噬是一种选择性自噬，特指细胞通过自噬机制特异性识别并清除受损、衰老或功能异常线粒体的过程。线粒体自噬具有高度选择性并依赖双重调节，主要分为PINK1/Parkin介导的线粒体自噬和受体介导的线粒体自噬［6，24］。

线粒体融合与分裂动态平衡保护创面

与机械性皮肤损伤比较，烧伤具有其特殊性，但创面愈合的核心病理过程是相似的，如炎症反应启动、细胞增殖迁移（成纤维细胞、角质形成细胞等）、组织重塑等。线粒体作为细胞能量代谢的核心枢纽，其分裂过程可通过两种方式优化能量供应：一方面，通过增加线粒体数提升整体产能效率；另一方面，通过分离损伤线粒体（使健康部分形成新的功能完整的线粒体）减少功能异常线粒体对能量代谢的干扰，从而满足细胞迁移和增殖过程中的高耗能需求。线粒体在烧伤创面愈合中主要表现为碎片化表型，即线粒体呈现更接近球形的形态且融合能力降低，因此线粒体分裂对烧伤创面愈合发挥重要作用［30］。Ponte等［31］研究发现，在果蝇胚胎损伤模型中，线粒体分裂可通过诱导伤口局部钙离子和活性氧水平升高、促进伤口边缘F-肌动蛋白聚合，进而加速伤口愈合进程，而DRP1会直接阻断这一过程，抑制伤口愈合。在线虫和斑马鱼等多种模型中，抑制线粒体分裂会阻碍伤口愈合，提示线粒体分裂对于伤口愈合的重要性［30，32］。而在果蝇胚胎损伤模型中，过度线粒体分裂并不会进一步促进伤口愈合，反而会引发活性氧和炎症因子过量产生，过度激活氧化应激和炎症反应，从而对伤口愈合产生不利影响［31］。在老化皮肤模型中，脂联素受体激动剂阿迪普隆（AdipoRon）可以通过抑制DRP1介导的线粒体分裂来抑制炎症和氧化应激，从而促进线粒体形态和功能恢复［33］。因此，适度的线粒体分裂有助于促进伤口愈合，而过度的线粒体分裂则会导致细胞无法抵抗随之产生的过度炎症反应和氧化应激，从而对伤口愈合进程产生不利影响。

相比之下，线粒体融合在创面愈合进程中发挥的作用似乎较为有限。但近期有研究显示，骨髓间充质干细胞在拓扑支架上培养时，其线粒体发生融合，在电镜下表现为线粒体面积增大、嵴长度增加，增强了骨髓间充质干细胞的氧化磷酸化能力；在动物实验中，拓扑支架上培养的骨髓间充质干细胞显著提高了烧伤创面的愈合率［34］。因此，线粒体融合对于烧伤创面愈合可能也具有一定益处。总之，在伤口愈合（包括烧伤创面愈合）过程中，线粒体融合与分裂的动态平衡是一个复杂且精密的调节过程，维持其动态平衡对改善创面损伤进展具有潜在作用［35-36］。

线粒体自噬抑制细胞凋亡保护创面

研究表明，烧伤后6 h瘀滞区微管相关蛋白1轻链3Ⅱ表达显著增加，且经透射电子显微镜证实存在线粒体自噬，可能与烧伤创面中HIF-1α表达上调而促进BNIP3和Parkin表达相关［2］。另有研究显示皮肤组织烧伤后PINK1、PRKN、MFN1和USP30等调节线粒体自噬的关键基因表达上调［11］，提示烧伤创面中存在线粒体自噬。进一步研究发现，线粒体自噬活性与创面细胞凋亡程度呈负相关：使用羰基氰化物-间氯苯腙诱导瘀滞区的线粒体自噬后细胞凋亡减少［2］。此外，刺激线粒体自噬的去铁酮（deferiprone）在烧伤模型中以BNIP3依赖的方式减少约95%的氧化应激［7］。上述证据表明，线粒体自噬可以通过减轻细胞凋亡和氧化应激延缓创面损伤进展。

在创面愈合止血阶段，功能活跃的线粒体是血小板活化的关键［37］。据报道，NIX控制的线粒体自噬是维持血小板活化的重要过程，基因消融NIX会严重损害缺陷线粒体清除，抑制血小板聚集和止血［38］。在缺血缺氧环境中，血小板中FUN14结构域蛋白1介导的线粒体自噬会促进血小板活化［39］。烧伤创面在典型的低灌注缺氧过程中，其血小板可能以相同的机制活化。在创面愈合炎症阶段，M1型巨噬细胞分泌多种促炎性细胞因子；早期炎症阶段M1型巨噬细胞产生线粒体活性氧并稳定HIF-1α，从而驱动促血管生成信号，这对于创面愈合至关重要［40］。在巨噬细胞向M1型极化时，NIX表达增加；而当NIX表达缺陷时，巨噬细胞向M1型极化受阻，提示NIX介导的线粒体自噬可能是巨噬细胞向M1型极化的重要条件［41］。在创面愈合增殖阶段，角质形成细胞通过增殖分化和迁移至创面重建表皮屏障，促进创面愈合［42-43］。研究表明，角质形成细胞分化成熟的最后阶段需要NIX介导的线粒体自噬参与，且BNIP3介导的线粒体自噬是角质形成细胞迁移的必备条件之一［44］。上述研究结果表明，线粒体自噬在延缓烧伤创面损伤进展及促进修复愈合方面具有重要作用。

靶向线粒体治疗在烧伤创面愈合中的应用

目前，靶向线粒体调控的分子在烧伤创面愈合中的研究已取得初步进展。PINK1和Parkin激活剂以及USP30抑制剂可以调节线粒体自噬，可能对烧伤患者创面愈合有益，但须注意过度清除线粒体及其对其他通路影响可能带来的潜在风险［45］。Chen等［46］发现褪黑素可通过腺苷酸活化蛋白激酶-转录因子EB信号通路激活Parkin依赖的线粒体自噬过程，并在动物研究中证实这一作用能够提高伤口愈合过程中皮瓣存活率。因此，对于烧伤后需接受皮瓣移植的患者，褪黑素可能具有积极的应用价值。HIF-1α在烧伤损伤中通过调节BNIP3或Parkin介导的线粒体自噬清除受损线粒体，降低氧化应激水平并减少细胞凋亡，从而减缓烧伤创面损伤进展，为创面修复及愈合争取时间［2］。辅酶Q10是线粒体呼吸链（电子传递链）的重要组成部分，参与复合体Ⅰ、Ⅱ和Ⅲ间的电子传递，是ATP生成的必需物质。其氧化形式（泛醌）与还原形式（泛醇）循环转化，可高效传递电子并维持线粒体氧化磷酸化的正常进行。在烧伤损伤中，辅酶Q10通过保护线粒体完整性减少线粒体DNA释放，从而抑制促炎性细胞因子（如IL-1β、肿瘤坏死因子-α）产生；还可调节线粒体的融合与分裂平衡，抑制线粒体形态异常（如肿胀、嵴结构破坏）［47］。法尼基转移酶抑制剂可以改善线粒体呼吸功能，并抑制烧伤引起的线粒体增大、嵴结构部分丢失，以及呼吸超复合体组装受损，恢复线粒体正常结构和功能［48］，有望改善严重烧伤患者的临床结局。

目前，靶向线粒体调控的分子治疗烧伤创面整体上仍处于基础研究阶段，存在诸多亟待突破的关键问题。未来可在以下几个方面进一步研究：第一，聚焦小分子调节剂的临床前研究，突破转化瓶颈。如针对PINK1、Parkin激活剂及USP30抑制剂开展大规模体外烧伤细胞模型实验，明确其特异性调控效果。第二，针对褪黑素开展小规模临床试点研究，明确其在烧伤皮瓣移植患者中的疗效、最佳给药方式、剂量及安全性。第三，深入探究分子间的协同调控机制，开发多靶点联合治疗策略。

结语

烧伤应激会对线粒体造成显著破坏，包括线粒体形态改变、ATP合成不足、线粒体呼吸受损以及线粒体活性氧产生增加等，维持线粒体融合与分裂的动态平衡、激活适度的线粒体自噬对减轻烧伤损伤、促进创面愈合具有重要意义。

尽管线粒体相关研究已取得一定进展，但针对烧伤创面中线粒体融合、分裂和自噬的系统性研究仍显匮乏。目前，线粒体融合与分裂的动态平衡主要通过调节OPA1和DRP1两大鸟苷三磷酸酶来实现，而这两种酶的激活同时也会激活其他通路，导致难以准确评估线粒体融合与分裂在烧伤创面损伤中的具体作用。同时，线粒体自噬在烧伤创面愈合各阶段的具体参与机制、动态变化规律及其与修复进程的关联尚不清晰，缺乏系统性的理论框架。基于当前的研究现状，未来亟须阐明烧伤后线粒体功能障碍的分子机制，揭示创面愈合过程中线粒体动态调控规律，从而为制订更有效的烧伤治疗策略提供科学依据。
